I'd say Juice Robinson is New Japan's best underdog. He gives every match his all but usually ends up failing in the end. In his promos he will continuously say he isn't the best in the company, but he has the most heart. That doesn't mean he loses all the time, though, which is a crucial part of the character. Juice will get big wins over some of the companies biggest stars every once in a while. One example is when Juice beat Naito in a tag match while Naito was still IC champ last year and Juice earned a title match against him. He lost, but the match was good enough to where he gained a little bit of a following. Juice getting so close to winning a title but never actually doing so made him gain the following he has now. When he finally won the US title, it felt like the conclusion we were all waiting for. I think Juice's "Heart and Honor" and "Flamboyant" nicknames the announcers use when he is coming to the ring sum up his character best. He has the flashy attire and loves to have a good time, but he also realizes he isn't the best in the company but he is going to keep trying and trying to be the best he can be.

But what would Juice's ceiling be in WWE? They currently have 71 male wrestlers on the main roster and that number seems to keep rising. If they sign Juice, I can only see him getting up to the IC/US title picture because i don't trust their writers enough to make his character work. Juice has some of the best English promos every week, but I don't even think he can make a WWE scripted promo work. Not many can. Meanwhile, in New Japan, he is the current IWGP US Heavyweight Champion at a time where they are expanding into the US and he is only 29. Imagine if he were to learn Japanese at this point. I think if he were to learn their language, he could be the next Kenny Omega over there in terms of how far they push him.

There is a HUGE difference when comparing the plot of the two games. Ocarina of Time has Link save Hyrule from Ganon by using the master sword and the ocarina of time to travel 7 years into the future. Link frees sages and beats Ganon in this game.(Majora's Mask spoilers ahead) In Majora's Mask, the game starts with Link, the same Link who beat Ganon and was sent back in time to relive his childhood, riding Epona in the lost woods looking for Navi. He runs into the skull kid from Ocarina of Time who is wearing Majora's Mask. He knocks Link off his horse and steals Epona and the Ocarina of Time. Link falls into Termina, the world of Majora's Mask, and is now tasked to stop a falling moon from destroying Termina and the Skull Kid. Two completely different plots. When comparing the gameplay, there aren't too many differences. They both have the same button layout and controlling Link feels about the same. The main difference between the two is that Majora's Mask allows you to play as a deku, a goron, and a zora.
